findings.summary: crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The coverage threshold refuses the real standard Steward bullet, and the criterion-4 demo uses invented bullet text, so the test does not cover critic finding 2
findings.evidence: Read in steward.rs:620-624: when a proposed change has no bullets, StewardRequest::from_change sets the acceptance to "The change is made as described: {title}", "No unrelated behavior changes; the existing tests pass" and "fmt, clippy and test pass". The demo for criterion 4 uses 'a test that fails before the change and passes after it', which does not appear in steward.rs. This job's own request has the real first bullet with a long title. By my hand count (an estimate, not run) it gives about 17 stems under the plan's stemmer and stop list: chang, mad, describ, read, drop, defer, part, multi, request, follow, job, onc, caught, final, verdict, correct, hand. ceil(17/2) = 9 of those stems must appear in one criterion. The accepted reading's best match, criterion 1, shares about 5 (read, part, request, follow, job). So the gate would refuse this job's own accepted reading, and any reading of a Steward-generated request with a long title. replay.rs:13 holds a candidate whose newly refused share exceeds what it declares, so the declared 5% is at risk. Fix: Build the Steward case from the real bullets: call StewardRequest::from_change, or copy steward.rs:621-623 verbatim with a realistic long title. Add this job's own request and accepted reading (both verbatim in the brief) as a corpus Accept case. Then change the rule so that case passes. Options: cap the required overlap (for example min(ceil(n/2), 3) distinctive stems); or, for the 'The change is made as described:' bullet, drop that prefix and match the title against the summary plus the criteria together. Keep a refuse twin so the acceptance is not vacuous.

findings.summary: The request-wide split exemption fires on common words, so many requests switch the check off by accident
findings.evidence: The plan exempts the whole request when any sentence contains a whole-word `split`, `separately`, `separate job` or `follow-up job` and no complaint cue. `split` is an ordinary code verb ('Split checks.rs into modules', 'split the parser') and `separately` is common prose ('test each form separately'). A request with parts (1)-(3) that says 'split the step list' would never have its parts checked. That fails open on exactly the failure class this job targets. The plan's only negative case is the complaint sentence; there is no case where `split` or `separately` is used in an ordinary sense. Fix: Count only permission phrasing about jobs or parts, for example 'may be split', 'can be split into separate jobs', '(N) can be a follow-up job' or 'in a follow-up job is fine'. A modal plus a job or part noun is required. Add corpus cases where `split` or `separately` appears in an ordinary sense and the deferral is still refused.

findings.summary: The 5% estimate has no stated basis, and the replay holds the change if the real share is higher
findings.evidence: The plan writes 5% into the doc comment and the CHANGELOG, but says nothing about where the number comes from. The planner cannot see records/, and the Steward-bullet counterexample above suggests the share could be much higher. replay.rs:293-301 holds a candidate that exceeds its declared share plus a margin. Fix: Label the 5% as an estimate and give its basis (for example, how many corpus Accept cases the new check refuses). Recheck the number after the threshold fix.
findings.location: Criterion 7 / checks.rs doc comment, 'expected 5% of newly refused readings'

findings.summary: Text that Athena's generators copy into requests can hold numbered lines that are not parts
findings.evidence: Requests built by hestia::root_cause_request and work_decisions::approve_request copy introspection or proposal text into the body. The refusal_corpus header (lines 22-27) shows check_defined_terms already treats such copied text as cited content. The plan skips only lines quoted with `>` and fenced blocks, so a copied '1. ... 2. ...' list would become required parts. Fix: Exclude generated cited spans the same way check_defined_terms does, or state that they are excluded and add a corpus case with a generated request that contains a numbered list.
findings.location: Decision 5 / Step 1 (numbered runs count anywhere outside quotes)

findings.evidence: The run rule depends on 'a stem in each entry', but the plan never says what makes a stem distinctive beyond surviving the stop set. With a short stop list, a stray '1. Yes 2. No' answer list would count as parts. Fix: Define it as at least one stem outside the stop set, with a minimum length, and pin it in a request_parts unit test.
findings.location: Step 1 ('each entry holds a distinctive stem')

request_reading_mismatch: The request asks that the stem rules let a criterion cover "the standard Steward bullet". The reading's criterion 4 defines the standard bullets as 'a test that fails before the change and passes after it; fmt, clippy and test pass; no unrelated behavior changes'. The bullets Steward actually generates (steward.rs:620-624), and the ones in this request's own Acceptance list, are 'The change is made as described: <title>', 'No unrelated behavior changes; the existing tests pass' and 'fmt, clippy and test pass'. The long-title 'as described' bullet is the hard case for stem matching, and the reading leaves it out.
summary: I read checks.rs (refusing_check and its step! macro), topics.rs (is_bullet, request_text_acceptance), steward.rs (from_change), replay.rs and the parser cases in refusal_corpus.rs. The plan's structure holds up. It adds a new step at the end of refusing_check, adds a separate request_parts parser so plan, steward and hestia acceptance stay unchanged, rewrites the two not-read-today cases, and leaves the reader rules unchanged within the budget. The named files, functions and line anchors exist. Two soundness problems need a revision. First, the plan's demonstration for criterion 4 uses bullet text I could not find in steward.rs, so it does not test the real standard Steward bullet. That bullet is "The change is made as described: <title>" (steward.rs:621). Under the ceil(n/2) threshold, a typical title would need about 9 of its stems to appear in a single criterion. By my hand count, this job's own request and accepted reading would then be refused. The replay at verification would probably also hold the change above its declared 5%. Second, the split exemption fires on bare common words such as `split` and `separately` anywhere in the request, so many ordinary refactoring requests would turn the check off. Smaller points: the 5% estimate has no stated basis, cited text that Athena's generators copy into requests can hold numbered lines, and "distinctive stem" is not defined.
